summary: Matches settlement, bank, and ledger records across sources, resolves what it can prove deterministically, and hands everything else to a human with a full replay of why it couldn't resolve it alone.

reads: Settlement recon data (Razorpay settlement recon API, or an equivalent CSV export)
Internal ledger / accounting export (merchant-uploaded CSV, e.g. Tally/QuickBooks-style)
writes: Its own local exceptions table (proposed matches and unresolved rows, pending human review)
Its own local narration_rules table (only after a human confirms a fuzzy match -- never written automatically)
never_reads_or_writes: Any merchant system outside the three sources explicitly listed above
No web scraping, no external inference, no unverified sources -- every value used in a match comes from a connected system or an uploaded file, never invented

can_do: Propose a match between a settlement, a bank credit, and a ledger entry
Categorize an unmatched row into a named exception type with a stated reason
Auto-apply a match only when both hold at once: confidence >= 0.90 AND the model tier that produced it is on an explicit trusted-tier allowlist
Record a human's confirm/reject/note decision against a specific row
Answer plain-language questions about the last run (order status, category counts, resolution rate) by reading the same persisted data, never inventing a figure
Quantify (not forecast) how much of a batch's exception-driven cash position this run resolved versus what's genuinely still open, computed from the same persisted net_amount/category/status columns
will_never_do: Post an entry to a real accounting system or settlement ledger -- this agent only proposes, a human or a separate posting system commits
Auto-apply any match from a tier not on the trusted-tier allowlist, regardless of reported confidence -- today that allowlist is empty, so nothing auto-applies at all
Modify a settlement record that has already settled
Take any action a human hasn't already granted it access to take

validation.module: src/validation_gate.py, separate from src/reconcile.py and src/llm_matcher.py
validation.gate_rule: auto_applied = (confidence >= CONFIDENCE_AUTO_ACCEPT) AND (tier in AUTO_APPLY_TRUSTED_TIERS); otherwise routed to human review
validation.audit_trail: Per-row structured replay_log (pass, action, confidence, timestamp, correlation_id) recording which pass resolved it and why, visible in the review queue
validation.idempotency: Re-running the same batch upserts on a stable match_key instead of deleting and reinserting -- a human's earlier confirm/reject decision is never erased by a later run (src/db.py)
validation.learned_pattern_guard: A human's confirm always succeeds, but a narration only gets memoized into the learned-pattern store if it contains a digit run unique to that order among every other order the agent has seen -- an overly generic confirm can't poison future auto-matching (src/db.py, _is_narration_specific)

human_control.review_surface: Local review website (src/review_server.py) -- confirm / reject / add-note per row
human_control.revocable: Deleting data/reconcile.db or not running the pipeline stops it entirely -- no persistent background process

known_limitations: Bank statement and internal ledger data are synthetic -- no live bank/Tally/QuickBooks API connected. Settlement side supports a real Razorpay API connection (src/ingest.py, run_all.py --live)
Ollama is excluded from the trusted-tier allowlist after testing showed a positional-bias failure mode -- see src/validation_gate.py
